title: A Lament for Tyre

questions.question: What does God command Ezekiel to raise over Tyre in chapter 27?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 27:2 (ESV): "Now you, son of man, raise a lamentation over Tyre,"

questions.question: How does Tyre describe herself in verse 3?
options: "I am the queen of the sea."
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 27:3 (ESV): "O Tyre, you have said, 'I am perfect in beauty.'"

questions.question: In the extended metaphor of the lament, what object is Tyre compared to?
options: An eagle flying over the sea
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 27 depicts Tyre as a beautiful, wealthy merchant ship built from the finest materials of many nations (planks of fir, mast of cedar, oars of oak, etc).

questions.question: Where did the builders get the fir tree planks for the ship of Tyre?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 27:5 (ESV): "They made all your planks of fir trees from Senir;"

questions.question: What wood was used to make the ship's mast?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 27:5 (ESV): "they took a cedar from Lebanon to make a mast for you."

questions.question: Where did the men of Tyre get their fine embroidered linen for their sail?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 27:7 (ESV): "Fine embroidered linen from Egypt was your sail, serving as your banner;"

questions.question: Who served as the rowers/mariners for Tyre's ship?
options: The inhabitants of Sidon and Arvad
The soldiers of Persia, Lud, and Put
questions.correctAnswer: The inhabitants of Sidon and Arvad
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 27:8 (ESV): "The inhabitants of Sidon and Arvad were your rowers; your skilled men, O Tyre, were in you; they were your pilots."

questions.question: What did the men of Persia, Lud, and Put do in Tyre's army?
options: They hung their shield and helmet in her to give her splendor
They manned the oars during battle
They rebuilt the breach in the walls
questions.correctAnswer: They hung their shield and helmet in her to give her splendor
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 27:10 (ESV): "Persia and Lud and Put were in your army as your men of war. They hung the shield and helmet in you; they gave you splendor."

questions.question: Tyre traded in many markets. What did Judah and the land of Israel trade for her merchandise?
options: Wheat, baked goods, honey, oil, and balm
Purple, embroidered work, and fine linen
questions.correctAnswer: Wheat, baked goods, honey, oil, and balm
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 27:17 (ESV): "Judah and the land of Israel traded with you; they exchanged for your merchandise wheat of Minnith, meal, honey, oil, and balm."

questions.question: What nation traded with Tyre for silver, iron, tin, and lead?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 27:12 (ESV): "Tarshish did business with you because of your great wealth of every kind; silver, iron, tin, and lead they exchanged for your wares."

questions.question: What happened to this glorious, heavily laden ship (Tyre) in the heart of the seas?
options: It ran aground on a hidden reef
Pirates set it on fire with flaming arrows
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 27:26 (ESV): "Your rowers have brought you out into the high seas. The east wind has wrecked you in the heart of the seas."

questions.question: When the ship falls into the heart of the seas on the day of her ruin, who falls with her?
options: Her wealth, wares, merchandise, mariners, pilots, caulkers, dealers, soldiers, and all her company
The king of Babylon and his commanders
The princes of Jerusalem seeking exile
questions.correctAnswer: Her wealth, wares, merchandise, mariners, pilots, caulkers, dealers, soldiers, and all her company
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 27:27 (ESV): "Your wealth, your wares, your merchandise, your mariners and your pilots, your caulkers, your dealers in merchandise, and all your men of war... fall into the heart of the seas on the day of your ruin."

questions.question: When the cry of the pilots is heard, what do all who handle the oar, the mariners and pilots of the sea, do?
options: Step down from their ships and stand on the shore
Leap into the water to save themselves
Raise a victorious shout to Babylon
questions.correctAnswer: Step down from their ships and stand on the shore
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 27:29 (ESV): "At the sound of the cry of your pilots the countryside shakes, and down from their ships come all who handle the oar. The mariners and all the pilots of the sea stand on the shore"

questions.question: How do the sailors mourn for Tyre?
options: They cry bitterly, cast dust on their heads, wallow in ashes, make themselves bald, put on sackcloth, and weep
They sing a dirge over a burnt offering
They cut themselves with swords until blood flows
They throw their oars into the sea and refuse to sail for a year
questions.correctAnswer: They cry bitterly, cast dust on their heads, wallow in ashes, make themselves bald, put on sackcloth, and weep
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 27:30-31 (ESV): "and wail aloud over you and cry out bitterly. They cast dust on their heads and wallow in ashes; they make themselves bald for you and put sackcloth on their waist..."

questions.question: What is the final terrifying conclusion of the lament regarding Tyre at the end of chapter 27?
options: "You have come to a dreadful end and shall be no more forever."
"Your sister city shall share your watery grave."
"The king of Babylon shall dwell in your palaces forever."
questions.correctAnswer: "You have come to a dreadful end and shall be no more forever."
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 27:36 (ESV): "The merchants among the peoples hiss at you; you have come to a dreadful end and shall be no more forever."

key_verse_text: "Your rowers have brought you out into the high seas. The east wind has wrecked you in the heart of the seas."
